designation: Abell 520, P3 ('dark peak') region (secondary / sensitivity source)

paper_found.authors: M. J. Jee, H. Hoekstra, A. Mahdavi, A. Babul
paper_found.title: Hubble Space Telescope/Advanced Camera for Surveys Confirmation of the Dark Substructure in A520
paper_found.journal_ref: ApJ 783, 78 (2014); DOI 10.1088/0004-637X/783/2/78 (confirmed on arXiv abs page)
paper_found.arxiv_id: 1401.3356 (e-print source ms.tex), re-downloaded independently into data/papers/groupE_jee2014_a520/

subcluster_designated: P3 of Jee et al. 2014 Table 1. The table has TWO P3 rows: 'P3 (old centroid)' (the J12 WFPC2 dark-peak location, no positional error) and 'P3' (new centroid)' (this ACS analysis, with bootstrap error). Both reported below.

z_cl.quote: This gives a plate scale of $\mytilde3.3$~kpc/$\arcsec$ at the redshift ($z=0.2$) of Abell 520. All the quoted uncertainties are at the 1-$\sigma$ ($\sim68$\%) level.

I.type: P3' (new centroid) — ACS weak-lensing mass (convergence) substructure centroid
I.location: Table 1 ('Mass Properties of Substructure (r<150 kpc)'), row P3'

uncertainty.location: Table 1 column header '$\Delta \alpha, \Delta \delta$ ($\arcsec,\arcsec$)' and table comment; Sect. 4.x 'Centroid and Significance of the Dark Peak'; Sect.1 says all quoted uncertainties are 1-sigma
uncertainty.quote: \tablecomments{The positional uncertainty is estimated from bootstrapping. ...} | Sect. 'Centroid and Significance of the Dark Peak in A520': "We measure the centroids using the first moments weighted by a circular Gaussian, whose FWHM matches the size of the substructure.  The results are displayed in Table~1.  The mean positional uncertainty is small ($\mytilde5\arcsec$)" | Sect.1: "All the quoted uncertainties are at the 1-$\sigma$ ($\sim68$\%) level."

alternate_row.type: P3 (old centroid) — J12 WFPC2 dark-peak centroid, used here as an aperture centre

G.quote: Interestingly, this new centroid is in better spatial agreement with the location where the X-ray emission is strongest
G.notes: No X-ray peak coordinates or I-G separation in arcsec/kpc are given anywhere in the paper. Gas masses in Table 1 are Cauchy-Schwarz upper limits in apertures, not positions.

S_candidates.label: none — P3/P3' is the 'dark peak' with no luminous cluster galaxies
S_candidates.quote: We examine the distribution of cluster galaxies and observe very little light at this location. | "The most critical substructure in A520 is the overdensity P3' ... between the two dominant mass peaks, where there are no luminous cluster members."

notes: Jee14 provides only weak-lensing (I) positions with per-axis bootstrap 1-sigma errors (P1, P2, P3', P4, P5); P3 (old) has no error. No X-ray peak (G) or galaxy/BCG (S) coordinates for P3/P3' or any other substructure. Table 1 header units: alpha,delta in (h m s, deg arcmin arcsec); Delta alpha, Delta delta in (arcsec, arcsec); Projected Mass in h70^-1 10^13 Msun; Gas Mass in h70^-5/2 10^13 Msun (90% CL upper limits). It is not stated whether Delta alpha is multiplied by cos(dec) (negligible at dec=+2.9 deg). Text states P3' is ~1 arcmin SW of P3 (old). Text (Sect. 'Comparison with C12') mentions 'the dark peak P4$^{\prime}$ appears $\mytilde99$\% of the random realizations' — apparently a typo for P3' (no P4' row exists). For the P4 (SW luminous subcluster) row see other_table1_rows_verbatim. Under the protocol: G and S missing -> unclassifiable from this source alone.
